hello.note: Both syllables rise; 'ho' is short, like 'hoe'.

good_morning.note: Literally 'morning'; a greeting on its own.

good_evening.note: Formal; nay ho does the job at any hour.

goodbye.note: 'joi' rhymes with 'boy'; bai-bai is as common.

slang.note: Everyday casual bye; fine for friends or a friendly stranger.

how_are_you.note: Textbook; friends ask sik jo faan may, 'eaten?'.

slang.note: Warm, phatic; family and close friends, not formal use.

thank_you.note: For service; 'm' is a hum. For a gift, daw jeh.

youre_welcome.note: Reply to thanks; 'never mind' is m gan yiu.

no_problem.note: 'Small matter'; brushes off thanks or an apology.

please.note: Formal; in practice a request just starts m goy.

excuse_me.note: To squeeze past; a plain m goy gets attention.

sorry.note: For a light 'oops', m ho yi si fits better.

yes.note: No plain 'yes'; this is 'it is'. Rhymes with 'eye'.

no.note: 'Not so'; to wave off an offer, m sai, 'no need'.

of_course.note: Casual emphatic yes; gang hai means 'certainly is'.

slang.note: Punchy praise for skill or effort; friends or a stranger.

delicious.note: 'Very tasty'; for a drink it is ho ho yam.

slang.note: General-purpose praise, food or otherwise; safe with anyone.

cheers.note: 'Drink to win'; gawn bui works too, as in Mandarin.
